references.text: God sends Moses to Pharaoh to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt, which is the same mission mentioned in Exodus 6:27.
Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh and speak to him on behalf of the Lord, as referenced in Exodus 6:27.
The Lord speaks to Moses and Aaron and gives them command to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt.
Identifies Aaron and Moses as those who were to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt, a direct precursor to verse 27.
The Lord gives Moses and Aaron instructions to speak to Pharaoh to let the children of Israel go.
Pharaoh calls for Moses and Aaron and lets the children of Israel leave Egypt, fulfilling the mission in Exodus 6:27.
The psalm mentions that God led his people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
God sent Moses, his servant, and Aaron whom he had chosen, to perform his signs in Egypt.
The Lord reminds Israel that he brought them out of Egypt and sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam before them.
In faith, Moses' parents hid him, and later in the chapter his role in the exodus from Egypt is described.
Stephen tells how God sent Moses as leader and deliverer to lead the people of Israel out of Egypt.
6:11 contains the actual command to speak with Pharaoh which Moses and Aaron later carry out (6:27).
7:2 explains the division of roles (Moses receives, Aaron speaks) that lies behind the expression 'it was Moses and Aaron' in 6:27.
Acts 7:40 is a direct allusion to the event described in 6:27, even though it reflects a misunderstood memory.
1 Sam 12:8 confirms and summarizes the entire exodus that Moses and Aaron began according to 6:27.
